stage_a.note: She is extremely positive, smiling constantly, and energetic throughout the pitch.
Very strong excitement about the product and its ability to solve the problem.

venture.description: Bright light therapy lamps that mimic the color and brightness of the sun to help set the body clock.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber delivers the prepared pitch for Circadian Optics, explaining the need for light therapy lamps in dark offices.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan asks Amber about her inspiration behind creating the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber states she is originally from Malaysia but currently lives in Minnesota.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark jokes that living in Minnesota explains her need for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber explains how the lack of sun in Minnesota led her to buy a lamp and eventually design a stylish one.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan notes her high valuation and asks if she has blockbuster sales to justify it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber confirms and states her lifetime sales are 7.4 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark expresses his dislike for lifetime sales figures.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan asks for her annual sales for the last twelve months.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber states she sold 4 million dollars last year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara asks if all of her sales are conducted online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber confirms that all of their sales are online.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara asks what her average online sale amount is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber states her average sale is 57 dollars and 99 cents.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks Amber what her profit margins are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber states her margin is 70 percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark infers she must be making a lot of money with those margins.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber begins to answer that she has been doing okay.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark challenges her, stating that with a 70 percent margin online, she should have huge returns unless something is wrong.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber clarifies that she made 652 thousand dollars last year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks what her projected sales are for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber states she is projected to do 5.6 million dollars this year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks what her profit will be on the 5.6 million dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber states she will make 1.3 million dollars after accounting for tariffs.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark notes this means she is making over 20 percent margins pre-tax.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber confirms her pre-tax margin is 25 percent.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks why she needs a shark given her success.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber explains she is looking for a strategic partner to help take the company into retail.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks Amber to share her personal backstory.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber tells the story of growing up poor in Malaysia and her parents cashing out their retirement to send her to America.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark reacts with amazement to her story.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber continues, explaining she survived toxic shock syndrome and decided to do something courageous by starting her business.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark praises her, saying she represents the American dream and freedom.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber thanks Mark for his kind words.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark shares his catchphrase about taking risks.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber repeats the catchphrase and laughs.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori praises her as someone who sees wishes instead of weeds and expresses a desire to invest.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark acknowledges Lori's statement.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks Mark if he would be interested in partnering with her on an offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark agrees he is open to it but suggests they hear more first.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan asks how he would get his money back as an outside investor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber states he will get his money back when the company scales.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan asks if she plans to give him 10 percent of distributions when she pays herself.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber states she is open to having that discussion.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara asks why she needs the money since she seems self-sufficient.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber explains the money will be spent on inventory and marketing for social media and their website.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Rohan praises her story but decides to exit as he does not see the value he could provide.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori announces that she and Mark will present their offer first.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori offers 750 thousand dollars for 20 percent equity, partnering with Mark.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber thanks them and asks to hear Barbara and Kevin's offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin offers 750 thousand dollars for 20 percent, partnering with Barbara, citing their ability to double sales.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori revises her and Mark's offer to include an extra 50 thousand dollars for Amber's parents.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin revises his and Barbara's offer to match the extra 50 thousand dollars for her parents.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark tells Amber she needs to make a decision.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amber accepts Lori and Mark's offer, stating she came to the show specifically for them.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori celebrates and congratulates Amber.

decisions.note: He does not see the value he could provide as an outside investor.
Partnering with Barbara Corcoran; claims they can double her sales and help with manufacturing.
Adding an extra 50 thousand dollars specifically for her parents.
Matching Lori and Mark's revision to include an extra 50 thousand dollars for her parents.
Accepts Lori and Mark's offer because she came to the show specifically for them.
